verdict.rationale: LiteLLM lets users configure specific event-triggered actions. Fallback rules reroute to another model group when a call fails after num_retries or raises a ContentPolicyViolationError, and logging supports custom callbacks that run custom code or hit API endpoints on request/exception events. These are fixed failure-handling and logging hooks, not a general rule engine where users define arbitrary event-to-action rules. Missing for 10: a general user-defined event→action rule engine, documented event types beyond failures and logging, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: If a call fails after num_retries, LiteLLM falls back to another model group, so a failing model or provider automatically fails over to a healthy backup.
